issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in searchTodos function. User-supplied keyword is directly interpolated into SQL query using template literal without parameterization or escaping.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized query: `const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE title LIKE $1 OR description LIKE $2'; const params = [`%${keyword}%`, `%${keyword}%`];` and pass params to db.query()

issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in searchTodosByStatus function. User-supplied completed parameter is directly concatenated into SQL query without type validation or parameterization.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized query: `const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE completed = $1'; const params = [completed === 'true' ? true : false];` to enforce type safety and prevent injection

issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in getTodosByUser function. User-supplied userId is directly interpolated into SQL query using template literal without parameterization.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized query: `const query = 'SELECT t.* FROM todos t JOIN user_todos ut ON t.id = ut.todo_id WHERE ut.user_id = $1'; const params = [userId];` and pass params to db.query()

codeQuality.summary: Three critical SQL injection vulnerabilities were introduced in the diff. All three new functions (searchTodos, searchTodosByStatus, getTodosByUser) bypass the secure parameterized query pattern used consistently throughout the rest of the codebase. These vulnerabilities allow attackers to execute arbitrary SQL commands. The existing code demonstrates the correct approach using parameterized queries ($1, $2 placeholders); the new functions must follow the same pattern.

suggestions.description: SQL injection vulnerability via unparameterized template literal with user-supplied keyword
suggestions.before:
const query = `SELECT * FROM todos WHERE title LIKE '%${keyword}%' OR description LIKE '%${keyword}%'`;
const rows = await db.query(query);
suggestions.after:
const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE title LIKE $1 OR description LIKE $2';
const rows = await db.query(query, [`%${keyword}%`, `%${keyword}%`]);
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates SQL injection risk by using parameterized queries, consistent with existing patterns in createTodo(), getTodoById(), updateTodoStatus(), and deleteTodo()

suggestions.description: SQL injection vulnerability via string concatenation with unvalidated completed parameter
suggestions.before:
const sql = "SELECT * FROM todos WHERE completed = " + completed;
const rows = await db.query(sql);
suggestions.after:
const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE completed = $1';
const rows = await db.query(query, [completed === 'true' || completed === '1']);
suggestions.benefits: Prevents SQL injection and adds type coercion to convert string input to boolean, matching updateTodoStatus() security pattern

suggestions.description: SQL injection vulnerability via unparameterized template literal with user-supplied userId
suggestions.before:
const query = `SELECT t.* FROM todos t JOIN user_todos ut ON t.id = ut.todo_id WHERE ut.user_id = '${userId}'`;
const rows = await db.query(query);
suggestions.after:
const query = 'SELECT t.* FROM todos t JOIN user_todos ut ON t.id = ut.todo_id WHERE ut.user_id = $1';
const rows = await db.query(query, [userId]);
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates SQL injection by using parameterized queries, aligns with secure patterns established elsewhere in codebase

refactorings.summary: Three critical SQL injection vulnerabilities introduced in the patch. The existing codebase (createTodo, getTodoById, updateTodoStatus, deleteTodo) demonstrates correct use of parameterized queries with db.query(query, params). The three new functions regress to unsafe string interpolation/concatenation patterns. All three require immediate refactoring to use parameterized queries with the same $1, $2 placeholder syntax used throughout the rest of the file.
